description: Society and population (ADR-005): from a place and an indicator to published income, poverty and inequality figures (poverty headcounts at stated lines, Gini and other inequality measures, income shares and medians), each with source, definition, release vintage and as-of time (World Bank PIP, Eurostat EU-SILC, OECD Income Distribution Database) side by side. Existing society-population providers (demographics, labour, education, housing, justice statistics) keep their bundles and ids.

profiles.description: Published income, poverty and inequality vocabulary

vocabulary.welfare concept: income or consumption, as the source states; never converted
vocabulary.equivalence scale: per-capita (PIP), modified OECD (EU-SILC) or square root (OECD IDD)
vocabulary.poverty line: the line the source publishes, with its PPP base year for absolute lines
vocabulary.vintage: one release of a series; a PPP revision restating past values is a new vintage
vocabulary.lineup estimate: a PIP reference-year estimate interpolated or extrapolated by PIP, labelled as such
vocabulary.comparability_unknown: two figures with no recorded difference or note; never assumed comparable

requires.reason: the bundle's own entry points use these operations
income values and vintages live in the Economics series storage
ISO, NUTS and World Bank region codes resolve to places through reviewable mappings
income monitors are knowledge subscriptions; shared provider reused, never duplicated
sources, licences and budgets are declared in the society-statistics source pack

optional_features.description: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform country estimates and regional aggregates at stated poverty lines and PPP rounds, each PIP release and PPP round a separate vintage (source worldbank-pip-poverty-inequality); deselecting it leaves EU-SILC and OECD answers unchanged

requires.reason: the worldbank-pip-poverty-inequality source of the society-statistics pack

optional_features.description: Eurostat EU-SILC at-risk-of-poverty rates, thresholds and Gini through the SDMX connector (source eurostat-eu-silc-income); deselecting it leaves PIP and OECD answers unchanged

requires.reason: the eurostat-eu-silc-income source of the society-statistics pack

optional_features.description: OECD Income Distribution Database indicators per methodology and income definition through the SDMX connector (source oecd-income-distribution-database); never mixed with EU-SILC values

requires.reason: the oecd-income-distribution-database source of the society-statistics pack

optional_features.description: Link income series to the Demographics denominators their sources name (economics.demographics); when not selected or absent the links are reported as feature_not_selected or provider_absent, and income answers are unchanged

requires.reason: denominators linked by citation or shared identifier

optional_features.description: Link income series to Labour indicators of the same place and period (economics.labour); when not selected or absent the links are reported as feature_not_selected or provider_absent, and income answers are unchanged

requires.reason: labour indicators linked by shared identifier or accepted place matches

exclusions: filling years a source did not publish
setting or applying poverty lines no source published
blending PIP, EU-SILC and OECD figures into one series
re-harmonising welfare concepts, equivalence scales or PPP rounds
deriving indicators (rates, shares or ratios) that no source published
never: fill a year a source did not publish
set a poverty line of our own
blend, average or rank PIP, EU-SILC and OECD figures as one series
convert income into consumption or re-base a PPP round
store or return person- or household-level data

query_examples.intent: Poverty and inequality in a country as of a date
query_examples.semantics: each source's vintage released by the date, side by side, grouped by line, PPP round and welfare concept, every value cited
every vintage with release dates, changed periods, PPP revisions and breaks
